findings.current: {family, select, wakes {जागृतियाँ} other {मॉनिटर}} वाली कुल {total} बातचीत में से {shown} दिखा रहे हैं।
findings.problem: Two case/number errors. The family arm is the direct plural, but the frame puts it before वाली, which takes the oblique (जागृतियों / मॉनिटरों; compare किताबों वाली अलमारी). The counted noun is singular where a numeral of two or more needs the plural, and में से needs the oblique plural: the shipped sentence renders कुल 42 बातचीत में से 10, not कुल 42 बातचीतों में से 10. The sidecar says the family select exists so the noun can take the form the sentence needs; it did not.
findings.replacement: {family, select, wakes {जागृतियों} other {मॉनिटरों}} वाली कुल {total, plural, one {# बातचीत} other {# बातचीतों}} में से {shown} दिखा रहे हैं।
findings.evidence: Rendered at four counts through the app's own parser: shipped 'जागृतियाँ वाली कुल 2 बातचीत में से 1 दिखा रहे हैं।' / '… कुल 42 बातचीत में से 10 …'; replacement 'जागृतियों वाली कुल 2 बातचीतों में से 1 दिखा रहे हैं।' / '… कुल 42 बातचीतों में से 10 …' / 'मॉनिटरों वाली कुल 9 बातचीतों में से 5 दिखा रहे हैं।'. node scripts/i18n/generate.ts --check exits 0 on the replacement (raising {total} to a plural is the escalation the generator's own comment permits for an inflecting noun). The remediation round must treat that kind escalation as reviewed, not as the auditor's strict kind comparison failing.

findings.problem: One English word, two Hindi renderings on one surface: the counter says चालू while empty.title and empty_line.monitors say सक्रिय. चालू also carries the 'running' sense that supervisor.not_running uses for the supervisor being down, so 'Monitors · 2 चालू' beside a sentence about चल नहीं रहा can read as the same claim. Two of the three occurrences already use सक्रिय.
findings.evidence: Rendered 'Monitors · 2 सक्रिय' and 'Monitors · 22 सक्रिय'; no placeholder or structure touched.

findings.current: …इसलिए नीचे दी जागृतियाँ नहीं जागेंगी। / …इसलिए नीचे दी जागृतियाँ केवल तब जागेंगी जब उनकी बातचीत चल रही हो।
findings.problem: नीचे दी जागृतियाँ drops the perfect participle; standard Hindi is नीचे दी गई जागृतियाँ. Core's committed Hindi uses the same elliptical नीचे दी उम्र in wire.settings, so this is a programme habit rather than a wave invention; the fix is local and correct here, and core can follow.
findings.replacement: …इसलिए नीचे दी गई जागृतियाँ नहीं जागेंगी। / …इसलिए नीचे दी गई जागृतियाँ केवल तब जागेंगी जब उनकी बातचीत चल रही हो।
findings.evidence: No placeholder or structure touched; the supervisor precedence the sidecar demands is unchanged.

findings.problem: At count 0 the CLDR hi rule selects one (Intl.PluralRules('hi').select(0) === 'one'), so this renders '0 जागृति' — a singular noun after zero, where '2 जागृतियाँ' is plural. The hi style guide records singular for zero ('one covers 0 and 1: "0 फ़ाइल" is singular'), core's committed Hindi ships the identical arms, and the second independent pass reads the singular as correct native Hindi, so this audit does NOT raise it to MAJOR even though a brief that classes a singular zero as major would. It is recorded as an open decision: if the programme prefers the plural reading, the verified replacement below needs no runtime change. Reachability: the count is entry.schedules.length (schedules-copy.ts:377) and the schema allows an empty array; show_more.* cannot render at zero (the control is gated on hidden > 0, schedules.tsx:385/456), and count.monitors / projects.sessions.count are unaffected because those nouns do not inflect in the direct plural.
findings.replacement: {count, plural, =0 {# जागृतियाँ} one {# जागृति} other {# जागृतियाँ}}
findings.evidence: Shipped renders 0 जागृति / 1 जागृति / 2 जागृतियाँ / 21 जागृतियाँ; the replacement renders 0 जागृतियाँ / 1 जागृति / 2 जागृतियाँ / 21 जागृतियाँ and node scripts/i18n/generate.ts --check exits 0 on it, so an explicit =0 arm is available without a code change.

The translator's identity and model were not visible to this auditor; independence is by agent and session, not by model diversity.
